clue.text: See 20
Six deliveries? Company put in too many!

blocks.note: in cricket an over is a set of six balls bowled
a crowd is a body of company, as in 'three's a crowd'

explanation.surface: A cricket over, then a complaint that a firm has packed in too many people.
explanation.walkthrough: An over in cricket is six deliveries by one bowler, a standard convention.
explanation.definitionFit: To overcrowd a space is to fill it with more people or things than it can comfortably hold.

clue.text: Gas in Middle English with Macbeth?

blocks.note: ME is the standard abbreviation for Middle English
Macbeth was Thane of Glamis and then of Cawdor

explanation.surface: A literary question about some gas in an old English text alongside Shakespeare's Scottish play.
explanation.walkthrough: A thane was a Scottish lord; Macbeth holds that title in the play.
explanation.definitionFit: Methane is a colourless flammable gas, the main component of natural gas.

clue.text: Scribe torn apart by dominie at last entering SCR

indicators.note: at last points to the final character of the preceding word only
entering means these pieces go inside the following letters

blocks.note: riven means split or torn apart
final letter of dominie
taken as written; the letters are split SC...R around the insert

explanation.surface: A clerk is mauled by a Scottish schoolmaster as he walks into the senior common room.
explanation.walkthrough: SCR is the senior common room of a college; a dominie is a Scottish schoolmaster. The inserted letters sit between C and R.
explanation.definitionFit: A scrivener was a professional copyist or clerk who wrote out documents, i.e. a scribe.

clue.text: Day Scottish man gets admitted to posh school in city

indicators.note: being admitted to a place means going inside it, so these letters sit within the school

blocks.note: D is the abbreviation for day
mon is Scots dialect for man
Eton is the famous English public school

explanation.surface: A Scotsman is admitted for a day to an elite school in some city.
explanation.walkthrough: Eton College is England's best-known fee-paying school.
explanation.definitionFit: Edmonton is the capital city of the Canadian province of Alberta, and also a district of London.

clue.text: One under pressure in the main – poor Eve despaired

definitions.text: One under pressure in the main

indicators.note: something poor is in a bad state, so the following letters are put into a damaged new order

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone is under pressure most of the time, and poor Eve has given up hope.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In the main' looks like 'mostly', but the main is the sea, and the pressure is water pressure.
explanation.definitionFit: A deep-sea diver works far below the ocean surface, enduring great water pressure.

clue.text: Warmer island for characters within Soay and Rhum?

indicators.note: characters within are the inner letters of each named word, leaving off the edges

blocks.note: the two inner letters of Soay
the two inner letters of Rhum

explanation.surface: Wanting a warmer island in place of two chilly Scottish isles.
explanation.walkthrough: Soay and Rhum are islands of the Scottish Hebrides, so a Pacific island is warmer than either.
explanation.definitionFit: Oahu is a Hawaiian island, home to Honolulu, with a tropical climate far hotter than Scotland's.

clue.text: Fish nets close to boats I'm capsizing in upheaval at sea

indicators.note: to net something is to catch it inside, so the fish encloses what follows
the close of a word is its final character, so only that is kept
a capsizing vessel turns over, so this word is read upside down in a down light

blocks.note: the tuna is a large sea fish
final letter of boats
taken as written, then turned round

explanation.surface: A fishing story: catches near the boats, and a fisherman overturning in rough water.
explanation.walkthrough: The fish holds the letter from boats, then I'm is turned round to MI.
explanation.definitionFit: A tsunami is a huge sea wave caused by an earthquake or other upheaval of the seabed.

clue.text: Relative in French city importing MDMA

indicators.note: a place importing goods brings them inside its borders

blocks.note: Nice is a city on the French Riviera
MDMA is ecstasy, commonly called E

explanation.surface: A family member caught bringing drugs into a city in France.
explanation.definitionFit: A niece is a kinship term: the daughter of one's brother or sister.

clue.text: Eye rat on the loose in bistro, say

indicators.note: something on the loose runs free, so these letters scatter into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A warning to keep an eye out for a rat running free in a small restaurant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Say' marks the bistro as one example of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: An eatery is any informal place to eat, and a bistro is one example of such a restaurant.

clue.text: Many layers shed?

blocks.note: surface reading: lots of coats or strata being peeled off or discarded
setter's reading: a shed that holds many laying hens

explanation.walkthrough: 'Shed' looks like a verb meaning cast off, but it is a noun, an outbuilding, and layers are egg-laying birds.
explanation.definitionFit: A henhouse is a hut where poultry roost and lay their eggs, so a shed full of layers.

clue.text: US special agents dash into bendy bus lane

indicators.note: going into something means being placed inside it
bendy means flexible and twisted, so the letters are bent into a new order

blocks.note: a dash or touch is a small amount, as of seasoning
taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Federal agents rushing into a bus lane, where a bendy bus is an articulated one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dash' looks like a rush, but it is a noun for a small amount; the rearranged bus lane splits around it.
explanation.definitionFit: The Untouchables were Eliot Ness's team of incorruptible Prohibition agents who pursued Al Capone.

clue.text: See 23
Worthless singing voice we hear

indicators.note: we hear signals that the word is judged by its sound when spoken

blocks.note: the bass is the lowest male singing voice

explanation.surface: A dismissive review of a singer's lowest register as worthless.
explanation.definitionFit: Base means of low value or quality, as in base metals, so worthless.

clue.text: Poem soldier oddly ignored

indicators.note: ignoring the odd-numbered positions keeps only the second, fourth and sixth characters

blocks.note: the even letters of soldier

explanation.surface: A poem about a soldier who was strangely overlooked.
explanation.definitionFit: An ode is a lyric poem, usually addressed to a particular subject in an elevated style.

clue.text: Nothing in Pan's Enigma worried religious movement

indicators.note: in places the first item inside the words that follow
worried means harried and shaken about, so the combined letters are jumbled

blocks.note: nothing is zero, which looks like O
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: The puzzle of the god Pan, troubling enough to spawn a religious movement.
explanation.walkthrough: Pan, the Greek nature god, fits the surface neatly, since neo-paganism revives such deities.
explanation.definitionFit: Neopaganism is a modern revival of pre-Christian nature worship, a religious movement such as Wicca.

clue.text: Using Latin to an offensive extent?

definitions.text: Using Latin to an offensive extent?

blocks.clueFragment: Using Latin to an offensive extent?
blocks.note: surface reading: someone overdoing the classical tags until it grates
setter's reading: a Latin phrase meaning to a sickening degree

explanation.walkthrough: The clue seems to mock someone who quotes Latin too much; in fact it asks for the Latin expression that itself means 'to a nauseating degree'.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin tag literally means 'to sickness', used of something repeated until it becomes tiresome.

clue.text: Watched fool getting tied up outside

indicators.note: being outside means wrapping around the item named first

blocks.note: a nit is a fool, short for nitwit
a boat tied up at a quay is moored

explanation.surface: Someone observed an idiot being bound and left outdoors.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tied up' looks like the fate of the fool, but it is the berthing word that goes around him.
explanation.definitionFit: To monitor is to observe or keep under surveillance, so watched is a synonym in the past tense.

clue.text: See 20
Chill overwhelms husband in ship or trains?

indicators.note: to overwhelm is to engulf and swallow up, so the first word surrounds the next
in places the combined letters inside the vessel

blocks.note: SS is steamship
to chill is to cool
H is the abbreviation for husband

explanation.surface: A cold spell swamps a married man aboard a ship, or perhaps on the railway.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Trains' looks like the railway rival to ships, but it is a verb meaning teaches.
explanation.definitionFit: To school someone is to educate or coach them, so schools works as a verb meaning trains.

clue.text: White end missing from magical rod

indicators.note: with its end missing, the final letter of the word is dropped

blocks.note: a wizard's wand is a magical rod

explanation.surface: A wizard's white wand that has lost its tip.
explanation.definitionFit: Wan means pale and sickly in colour, so white in the face.

clue.text: For which frantic US team swoops? Finds no trace?

definitions.text: For which frantic US team swoops? Finds no trace?

indicators.note: frantic means wildly agitated, so all the letters that follow are thrown into disorder

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: American inspectors raid site after site and turn up nothing.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both the anagram and the definition: it recalls the 2003 Iraq war, when US searches for banned arms found none.
explanation.definitionFit: Weapons of mass destruction are nuclear, chemical or biological arms, the alleged Iraqi arsenal that searchers never found.

clue.text: London section starts to spy on Home Office

indicators.note: the starts of words are their opening characters, one taken from each

blocks.note: initial letters of spy, on, Home and Office

explanation.surface: Part of London where agents begin snooping on the Home Office, Britain's interior ministry.
explanation.definitionFit: Soho is a district of the West End of central London, known for nightlife and theatres.

clue.text: Cook involved in fiscal drag

indicators.note: involved in says the letters are wrapped up inside the words that follow

blocks.note: the run of letters across the end of the first word and start of the second

explanation.surface: A chef caught up in the economics of fiscal drag, where inflation pushes earners into higher tax bands.
explanation.definitionFit: To scald is to heat a liquid, such as milk, to just below boiling, a cooking technique.

clue.text: Drink substantial UAE factory ships back

indicators.note: a vessel ships cargo by carrying it inside, so the words that follow hold the letters
back means the carried letters are read from right to left

blocks.note: the letters run across the end of substantial, all of UAE and the start of factory, then are turned round

explanation.surface: A big Emirati plant exports a beverage back home.
explanation.definitionFit: Café au lait is French for 'coffee with milk', a hot drink of coffee and steamed milk.

clue.text: Such a vile man – I'm possibly a product of this?

definitions.text: Such a vile man – I'm possibly a product of this?

indicators.note: possibly signals one of several arrangements, so the preceding letters are recombined

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A sexist man muses that his own vileness may be the result of his attitudes.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both definition and anagram: the letters before 'possibly' rearrange to the attitude that produces such a man.
explanation.definitionFit: Male chauvinism is the belief that men are superior to women, the attitude behind a sexist man's behaviour.

clue.text: A scruffy old bear inspiring great affection

indicators.note: something scruffy is untidy and dishevelled, so these letters are put in disarray

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A shabby old teddy bear that is much loved.
explanation.definitionFit: Adorable means lovable or charming, so it describes something that inspires great affection.

clue.text: Painter concerned with dark film genre

blocks.note: re means regarding or concerning
film noir is the dark crime-movie genre

explanation.surface: An artist preoccupied with gloomy crime movies.
explanation.definitionFit: Pierre-Auguste Renoir was a French Impressionist artist; his son Jean was a film director.

clue.text: Hand out is with soft thick sandwiches

indicators.note: a sandwich has bread on both sides, so the outer word encloses what precedes it

blocks.note: dense means thick, as fog or a crowd
taken as written
p is piano, the musical term for soft

explanation.surface: Someone distributes soft, thick sandwiches.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sandwiches' looks like food being handed out, but it is a verb, the enclosing signal.
explanation.definitionFit: To dispense is to distribute or give out, as a pharmacist dispenses medicine.

clue.text: Adult thought provoked a snigger

blocks.note: A is the film classification for adult
to muse is to ponder, so mused means thought

explanation.surface: A grown-up's reflection drew a stifled laugh.
explanation.definitionFit: To amuse is to make someone laugh, so amused, past tense, matches drawing a snigger from them.
